finding: V20 cannot safely be implemented by merely removing task.cancel() or shielding one await. Once provider-side work has begun, the provider->canonical-response->strict-durable-publication transaction must have an owner independent of the SSE generator/client connection. The current stream_openai_responses creates run_request as a local task and unconditionally cancels it in generator finally when unfinished. There is no server-level registry/lifecycle owner for such commit-critical tasks.
risk: If the client disconnects after the provider has advanced but before durable publication, cancelling or losing ownership of the local task leaves no durable replay record. A retry can then call the provider again. Conversely, simply leaving an unowned task running makes exception observation and application shutdown semantics undefined.
required_invariant: Before provider start, client cancellation may cancel the request.
After provider start, client/SSE lifetime must not cancel the commit-critical transaction.
A server-level strong-reference registry must own commit-critical tasks until completion and consume/log exceptions.

Application shutdown must explicitly drain commit-critical tasks for a bounded interval; if safe durable publication cannot finish, shutdown/recovery must fail closed rather than report the request as safely replayable.
No response/call/reasoning IDs or provider-derived content may be emitted before strict durable publication under the combined V12+ stream rules.
